title: Rust Graph, Analysis and Transactional Mutation Core

preflight.note: Created before Rust graph, deterministic analysis, mutation planning/application, or mutation-parity implementation begins; implementation is gated on WI053 conformance evidence.

acceptance_criteria.text: Define a typed Rust relationship graph for work items, dependencies, acceptance criteria, evidence, scopes, decisions, applicable contracts/invariants/frozen surfaces where derivable, provenance/review relations, and reverse references without inventing authority absent from canonical records.
Graph queries are deterministic and return source record/path context sufficient for clients to explain why a relationship exists.

Implement deterministic repository analyzers for next work-item ID, overlapping work, scope ownership/overlap, dependency candidates/reverse dependencies, frozen-surface impact, related decisions, unresolved findings, applicable contracts, evidence gaps, and provenance/review concerns where those facts are derivable.
Analysis findings identify the concrete repository facts that caused them; opaque scores or provider output alone are not accepted as governance explanations.

Define a typed `MutationRequest -> MutationPlan -> MutationResult` boundary that validates requested changes, computes all durable/generated impacts, produces diagnostics and a canonical preview/diff, and requires explicit apply against the repository state used to create the plan.
Mutation plans carry repository/state preconditions and are rejected as stale when materially relevant repository state has changed before apply.

Supported mutation application is atomic or recoverable, uses canonical serialization, regenerates owned derived projections, and performs post-write validation before success is reported; tests cover failures before/during multi-file apply and cleanup/recovery behavior.

Implement supported work-item creation/edit/lifecycle/dependency/acceptance-criterion operations needed by the future desktop workflow while preserving current governance, preflight, lifecycle, dependency, and evidence rules.
Decision/evidence mutation support, if implemented, preserves existing durable-history and evidence immutability semantics; completed evidence is never exposed as a generic overwrite operation.
Add executable cross-implementation before/after parity fixtures for every mutation/generation surface whose authority moves to Rust; success-message parity alone is insufficient.
No native/desktop/future client is required to directly write governed RepoPact records; supported writes are available through the core mutation boundary.

Any assisted-analysis extension boundary remains provider-neutral and proposal-only; no LLM/provider dependency enters RepoPact authority and provider output cannot activate work, waive criteria, approve frozen changes, fabricate authorization, or bypass validation.
WI050 admission/guard/enforcement remains outside this work item and existing fail-closed security behavior is neither ported nor weakened as a side effect of the new mutation API.

Closeout evidence lists supported graph queries, analyzers, mutations, parity fixtures, recovery tests, generated projections, known unsupported mutations, and confirmation that Tauri/Python cutover/WI050 migration remain separate work.
